transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-09-10
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 mins
Attendees: Alex Grant (Redwood AE), Priya Kulkarni (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (NexaHealth CTO), Marta Alvarez (NexaHealth ML Eng), Samir Patel (NexaHealth Dev)
Shared: deck: https://redwood.ai/deck/hosted-api-demo (shared), security doc link noted

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex grant from redwood, i'll kick off, priya's going to deep-dive on the demo
[00:18] Jordan: yep, thanks, quick note—we only have 45-50 minutes, we want to focus on streaming and retries, and, uh, cost implications
[00:32] Priya: great, we'll prioritize that. quick intro—NexaHealth, you mentioned latency SLOs of ~200ms p95 for short chat, is that still right?
[00:45] Jordan: yes, for user-facing assistant, p95 below 250ms ideally. for some background jobs we can accept more latency
[00:53] Priya: ok got it. quick agenda: API basics, streaming demo, params (max_tokens, temperature, top_p), retry/backoff patterns, console and optimize suggestions, q&a

[05:12] Priya: demo time—i'm in the console, navigating to "Hosted API" -> chat endpoints. you can see model catalog, we picked "rw-medium-v1" for this demo, it's a good balance for short chat
[05:30] Samir: is rw-medium-v1 the same as the open model you guys host or is that a proprietary variant?
[05:35] Priya: it's a curated open model variant that we've validated on latency/cost; we also offer quantized variants on dedicated pools

[08:04] Priya: starting the streaming example—i'll call the chat endpoint with streaming=true. note the SDK shows on_stream callback, and the console has a live stream log
[08:21] (transcription glitch) Speaker 2: streaming looks... stringing? sorry
[08:29] Priya: yeah transcription clipped, but you can see tokens arrive in chunks, client can render partials, and we support HTTP chunked + websocket streaming
[09:05] Priya: important params—max_tokens (controls generation length), temperature (sampling), top_p (nucleus sampling). show a quick before/after: temp 0.0 vs 0.8
[09:22] Marta: so lower temp => deterministic, good for instructions, high temp => creative, got it

[12:40] Priya: retries—two main patterns: client-side retry idempotency keys for non-streaming requests, and streaming fallback to short reconnects. for streaming we recommend resume-token pattern or fall back to non-streaming single-call
[12:58] Jordan: what's the best practice for dedup? if we retry early do we risk double-processing?
[13:10] Priya: yes, use idempotency keys on generate calls. for chat we suggest stateless request ids at the router, and server will detect duplicate id and return same response
[13:28] Alex: also, for long-running responses we have a timeout and an error code that indicates partial content; client should handle resume or call with same id to get remaining tokens

[17:05] Priya: sdk example in python: client.chat.create(..., streaming=True, on_stream=callback, max_tokens=150, temperature=0.2). note we include built-in exponential backoff helper in the SDK
[17:22] Samir: do you have code for exponential backoff that handles 429s and 5xx?
[17:28] Priya: yes, we handle 429 with jittered backoff, for 5xx we differentiate transient vs fatal; we'll send the snippet after the call

[20:02] Priya: cost conversation—batching and caching: for repeated prefixes we recommend prefix KV cache on dedicated or use our caching layer on hosted for common prompts; Optimize shows suggestions like lowering max_tokens or using a smaller model for non-critical flows
[20:20] Jordan: curious about token accounting—do you charge for prompt+generated tokens? what about streaming overhead?
[20:32] Alex: yes prompt + completion counted. streaming doesn't change billing units, it's per-token. small overhead for latency but not billed separately

[24:50] Priya: Console demo: routes page, per-route token/latency breakdown, spikes view. you can set per-route model overrides (route to rw-small for low cost flows)
[25:12] Marta: can we create an A/B test in the console to route 10% to a cheaper model?
[25:20] Priya: yeah, rollout -> canary -> percentage split, and you can set automatic fallback if latency or error rate exceeds threshold

[28:40] Priya: Optimize suggestions—our service will analyze recent traffic and recommend quantization or batching changes. example: for your conversational workload we'd suggest synced batching window of 10-30ms and a quantized variant that reduces cost ~30%
[29:05] Jordan: great, do you run regressions on quality when quantizing?
[29:12] Priya: yes, Optimize runs evals against your prompt set and warns if quality drops beyond a threshold; you can pin baseline and auto-rollback

[33:00] Alex: security quick notes—SOC 2, SSO/SAML, VPC peering for Private, and customer-managed keys via KMS. you asked about logs and retention
[33:14] Jordan: we need audit logs for 1 year and data residency in us-east
[33:25] Alex: that's fine—hosted supports region selection and we can include longer retention under enterprise plan, we'll share the security whitepaper

[36:40] Priya: performance note—if you need stricter latency SLOs, dedicated pools give predictable p95 and you can reserve capacity. hosted is fine for many apps but dedicated reduces noisy neighbor issues
[36:58] Marta: if we go dedicated, is there an easy migration path?
[37:05] Priya: yes same API surface, you just select dedicated org model in route rules; plan change is primarily billing/account work

[40:15] Jordan: ok next steps—we want to run a short pilot: 1k concurrent chat sessions, target p95 200-250ms, and we'd like Redwood to run a benchmark
[40:28] Alex: we'll put together a pilot proposal with committed capacity options and pricing tiers
[40:35] Priya: i'll share SDK snippets, backoff examples, and a checklist for sample data

[42:50] Alex: recap: Alex to send pricing and pilot proposal; Priya to send SDK snippets and security docs; Jordan to provide sample prompts and target metrics; schedule benchmark call for next week
[43:20] Jordan: sounds good, thanks
[43:30] Marta: thanks all
[43:40] (end)

Notes: transcription has occasional mislabels and clipped words. References: demo deck, security whitepaper, code notebook link to be shared.
